headline: ERS joins coalition urging COP31 to put healthcare workers at centre of climate and health initiative
dek: The European Respiratory Society is one of 18 health professional networks asking the COP31 Presidency to add a health workforce pillar to its new Antalya Initiative for Resilient Health Systems.
body:
The European Respiratory Society (ERS) is part of a coalition of 18 leading networks of health professionals calling on the COP31 Presidency to place healthcare workers at the heart of its new climate and health initiative, ERS said on X and on its website.

The coalition encourages the creation of a dedicated health workforce pillar within the Antalya Initiative for Resilient Health Systems (AIR). According to ERS, AIR is a new drive under the COP31 Action Agenda to strengthen countries' ability to prepare for, respond to and adapt to climate-related health threats. COP31 is taking place this month in Antalya, Türkiye.

ERS also co-hosted a side event on 12 November with the European Youth Energy Network, titled 'One breath, one planet: clean air, climate action and asthma'. Part of the COP31 Health Pavilion programme, it highlighted the health benefits of climate action and clean air policies, including reduced air pollution, fewer respiratory conditions and less pressure on health systems. ERS said the discussion concluded with three policy actions needed to protect respiratory health and advance climate and clean air action.

On the same day, Prof. Zorana Jovanovic Andersen, chair of the ERS Advocacy Council, took part in a panel on black carbon organised by the World Health Organization, the International Society for Environmental Epidemiology and Wellcome Trust. The panel moved from scientific evidence to practical action.

ERS has additionally endorsed the Global Climate and Health Alliance's Health Community Policy Recommendations. These call on Parties at COP31 to recognise climate change as a leading threat to health and to act to protect health across all negotiations. The recommendations also describe co-benefits of climate action, such as prevention of non-communicable diseases including asthma and COPD.
key_quote: ERS is part of a coalition of leading health professional organisations to call on the COP31 Presidency to place healthcare workers at the centre of its new climate and health initiative.
